exposure: Call schedule type (traditional vs. night float)
Women attempting trial of labor after cesarean
Obstetrician call schedule (traditional vs. night float)
outcome: Likelihood of attempting trial of labor after cesarean (TOLAC)
Likelihood of achieving vaginal birth after cesarean (VBAC)
Maternal outcomes (uterine rupture, chorioamnionitis, postpartum hemorrhage)
Neonatal outcomes (admission to neonatal intensive care unit)
cohort: 1502 women with 1 prior low transverse cesarean delivery and a term, cephalic singleton gestation
finding: Women cared for by physicians with a night float call schedule were significantly more likely to undergo TOLAC and achieve VBAC.
mod_finding: While women delivered by providers with a night float schedule were initially more likely to experience uterine rupture, chorioamnionitis, postpartum hemorrhage, and neonatal intensive care unit admissions, these associations did not persist when limited to women who attempted TOLAC.
